topic: Analyzing traffic detection and data parameters
summary_markdown: The discussion focused on refining traffic detection logic, particularly for vehicles like buses and bicycles. Initial plans involved analyzing traffic passing by the curb and potentially segmenting data by transport type (e.g., separating bicycle counts). Concerns were raised about inaccurate object detection, where a single vehicle might be counted as multiple objects due to partial visibility (e.g., detecting only the cabin and end of a bus). To improve accuracy, it was proposed implementing a rule requiring two synchronized points at a specific distance (e.g., 6 meters) for an object like a bus, with no other detected objects between those two points. This method aims to prevent false positives in congested areas.
decisions: The initial focus will be on simple detection cases before adding complexity.
A proposed logic involves detecting two synchronized points at a set distance (e.g., 6 meters) for large vehicles like buses, ensuring no other objects are detected between them.
